ruling.recommended_action: Close the case: the sole off-route segment is covered by the rider's own pre-segment general routing authorisation; no refund due under RD-2. No account action (RD-6 precondition unmet).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI Jurong Point → Suntec City, 30.0 km against a 24.4 km optimal route (+5.6 km) and 48.3 min against a 33.6 min estimate, charged $60.30 on the meter [F1][F2][F7]. Under RD-1 every off-route segment must be individually checked against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and only an unexempted segment is refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2]. The trace confirms exactly one off-route segment, F3 (13:07–13:19, 7.41 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km, up to 1391 m off corridor) [F3].

RD-4 gives no cover: the trace marks (a) failed and the record shows no traffic incident near the route in the trip window [F15], while the only speed-band evidence is AER band 2 for 12:41–13:07, which stops exactly as the segment begins and is, per RD-4(b)/G3, insufficient on its own to exempt a segment [F12][F3][RD-4].

The decisive question is RD-5 consent: the driver asked at 13:03 whether to take another way because traffic on the AER was building up, and the rider replied at 13:04 "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" — both messages timestamped in a complete two-message record, i.e. before the segment began at 13:07 [F8][F9][F10]. That is a general route choice, not consent to a named road: F8 names only the road to be avoided and no rider message names a road to be taken, so no named-road tie exists to trigger G13 [F8][F9]. A general authorisation covers a route chosen to reach the destination and excludes only the driver's own affairs — a stop away from the route or a loop that reaches nothing; here no stop, errand or detour-specific purpose of the driver's own appears anywhere in the record, so the loop does not fall within that carve-out and the segment is exempt [F9][F3][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement is a claim, not rider consent, and is not needed [F11][RD-5].

Because the only off-route segment is exempt, no unexempted segment remains for RD-2, and the metered excess (billed as $7.88, 5.59 km × $1.4101/km) is not refundable [F4][F7][RD-2]. The other line items are untouched: the $0.11 is a metered RydeTAXI waiting unit (0.4 min × $0.26/min), which RD-3(c) keeps with the driver and which the rider does not claim, no surge applied (multiplier 1.0×), and the $1.47 platform fee is a published fee — none generates a refund [F5][F6][F7][RD-3][FARE-1]. RD-6 does not attach: no RD-1 breach is recorded and the driver's 90-day route-upheld count is 0 [F18][RD-6]. Amount is therefore $0.00, i.e. no_action.

Evidence is complete for everything the ruling needs: the complete timestamped chat, the single measured segment, the fare breakdown and the traffic screens are all present [F3][F4][F7][F10][F15]. Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement in context — the complaint is a fare/meter grievance, F8/F9 are a route-and-lateness exchange, and F11 merely recounts traffic; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11].

The words are a general route choice ('whichever way is faster' for reaching the destination), not a named road, so G13's tie requirement is not engaged; no rider message asks for a stop or the driver's own errand, and no fact places a stop, errand or loop-to-nowhere purpose inside the segment, so the general authorisation covers the route driven [F3][F9][RD-5]. Segment exempt, no RD-2 refund.

Accepted that F3 is the sole off-route segment and that RD-1 makes an unexplained deviation a breach [F3][RD-1]; but the deviation is explained by the rider's own pre-segment general authorisation [F8][F9], so it is exempt, not unexempted [RD-5].

The rider's own words in F9 are a general route choice covering the route to the destination; the errand/loop-to-nowhere carve-out requires a stop or purpose of the driver's own, and no fact records one in the 13:07–13:19 segment [F9][F3][RD-5].
Correct that F15 records no incident and that F12's band alone cannot exempt a segment [F15][F12][RD-4]; the exemption here does not rest on RD-4 but on rider consent under RD-5 [F8][F9][RD-5].
Conceded arithmetic: the billed excess and the fare breakdown are as stated [F4][F7]; but billed kilometres on a consented corridor are not refundable [F9][RD-2][RD-5].
The $7.09 formula runs only on an unexempted segment [F3][F4][RD-2]; the segment is exempt, so the refundable mileage is 0 km.

No road to be taken was named by either party, so no named-road tie exists and G13's undetermined finding is not triggered; a general authorisation is read as general_route_consent, not undetermined [F8][F9][F3][RD-5].
RD-6 requires a case upheld against the driver plus a prior upheld route dispute; the driver's 90-day route-upheld count is 0 and no breach is recorded here, so no flag attaches [F18][F17][RD-6].

The $7.88 billed excess is not, as claimed, the maximum meter exposure of the off-route segment; it is the whole trip's excess above the optimal distance, whereas RD-2 would refund only an unexempted segment's own extra_km [F4][F3][RD-2]. The point does not affect the outcome because the segment is exempt.
